title: Locality of the polynomial algebra adjoining p-th roots
statement: Let p be prime, A a commutative local F_p-algebra, n a natural number and a : Fin n → A. Define B = A[X_i]/(X_i^p-a_i), using [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Then B is local and A → B is a local ring homomorphism. The polynomial quotient is the actual construction Algebra.pthRootAlgebra; no arbitrary field or ring is chosen. The empty family is allowed.

source.place: Tag 07E5, proof of (2) => (4); read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07E5 because the local literature checkout is absent. The local quotient argument is the general finite p-root version of the local-base-change construction, expanded by P3 using monic division, integral contraction and Frobenius uniqueness. Also Algebra Tags 00GQ (lying over) and 0BR8 (uniqueness from powers in the image), read online.

proof.text: Let K be the residue field of A and Ω its algebraic closure. Compose the residue map with K → Ω. By IsAlgClosed.exists_pow_nat_eq choose roots α_i of the images of a_i. MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom at α_i annihilates every generator X_i^p-a_i and therefore the entire defining ideal, by Ideal.span_le. Ideal.Quotient.lift gives a homomorphism g:B → Ω. Since Ω is a field, g.domain_nontrivial makes B nontrivial. The composite A → B → Ω equals A → K → Ω on every coefficient.

The map F_p → A → B gives characteristic p on nontrivial B, by CharP.of_ringHom_of_ne_zero. Each defining relation gives q(X_i)^p = a_i. Prove that every b in B has b^p in the coefficient image: lift b along the quotient map and use MvPolynomial.induction_on. Constants use map_pow; sums use add_pow_char; multiplication by X_i uses mul_pow and the defining relation. No finite-freeness, integral extension, or prime-ideal argument is needed.

For b in B choose c in A with c mapped to b^p. IsLocalRing.isUnit_or_isUnit_one_sub_self applied to c gives that c or 1-c is a unit. Their images are b^p and (1-b)^p, respectively, using sub_pow_char. Apply isUnit_pow_iff, since p>0, to conclude that b or 1-b is a unit. IsLocalRing.of_isUnit_or_isUnit_one_sub_self gives locality of B. No variable occurs in this criterion, so the empty family is included.

Suppose the image of x in B is a unit. Its image under g is a unit in Ω and hence is nonzero. If the residue of x in K were zero, the composite identity on coefficients would make this image zero. Thus the residue is nonzero, and IsLocalRing.residue_ne_zero_iff_isUnit shows that x is a unit. This is exactly IsLocalHom.map_nonunit for A → B.

proof_origin.place: Tag 07E5, construction of A' in (2) => (4), with the power-in-coefficient-image observation of Algebra Tag 0BR8. P4 gives a shorter direct unit-criterion proof, using Mathlib's algebraic closure, polynomial induction, Frobenius identities, and local-ring criterion. Both source tags were read online on 2026-10-13.

lean.statement:
theorem pthRootAlgebra_local (p n : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime]
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra (ZMod p) A] [IsLocalRing A]
    (a : Fin n → A) :
    ∃ hlocal : IsLocalRing (pthRootAlgebra p n A a),
      letI := hlocal
      IsLocalHom (algebraMap A (pthRootAlgebra p n A a))
